sections.html:
Pembroke Pines sits in southwest Broward and has more than 170,000 residents. It has easy reach of major highways, jobs, parks and golf courses. The city was incorporated on January 16, 1960 as the Village of Pembroke Pines with about 1,500 residents, and after Hurricane Andrew in 1992 it became one of the fastest growing cities in the country. That is why so much of its housing dates from the 1990s and later.

Buyers range from families drawn by schools and parks to residents of the Century Village area. Knowing your home's age helps you decide whether a cash offer or a listing fits.

sections.h2: House age by side of town
sections.html:
Land west of US 27 was annexed by 1981, so house age varies by side of town. Fire stations opened as the city expanded: Station 79 in 1981 on the annexed land and Station 89 in 1986 at Century Village.

  • Check roof, electrical and plumbing age on your own house.
  • Ask a title agent what recorded items exist on your lot.
  • Keep permit and inspection records ready for a buyer's inspector.

sections.h2: What Florida charges to transfer a house
sections.html:
The deed rate is 70 cents per $100 of consideration, and each party to the document is liable.

Which documents carry stamp tax on a real estate transfer
DocumentStamp tax applies?
Warranty deedYes
Quit claim deedYes
Deed in lieu of foreclosure saleYes
Personal representative deed under probated willNot taxable

The clerk of court collects the tax when recording. Ask your closing agent to apply the rate to your price in writing.

The Broward property appraiser values property on January 1 and takes exemption filings through March 1. Call 954-357-6830 with questions.

  • August brings the proposed tax notice.
  • November bills carry the largest early payment discount, 4 percent.
  • April 1 marks delinquency.

Your closing agent splits the year's tax between you and the buyer, so confirm the split reflects your exemption status.

sections.h2: Homestead and portability if you move
sections.html:
It matters most after many years of ownership. Save Our Homes has kept your assessment growth at 3 percent or CPI, whichever is lower, and portability may move up to $500,000 of the savings to a new Florida home.

The new homestead has to begin within three years of the January 1 that follows the old one being given up. Form DR-501T goes in with the DR-501 by March 1. Later amendments first apply to the 2027 roll, so call the appraiser to confirm current rules.

Each situation runs on a clock. Estates with up to $150,000 non-exempt can use summary administration, creditors file within three months of publication or 30 days of service, whichever is later, and foreclosure sales follow judgment by 20 to 35 days.

Tenants receive a 3 day nonpayment notice and 7 days to cure many breaches. These facts affect offers, so assemble the documents first.

The city's fire rescue department began as a volunteer group in 1953, hired its first three full-time employees in 1973 and now runs six stations. Pembroke Pines became the South Region answering point in the Broward County Regional 911 system in 2014. Buyers care about response times and insurance ratings, so ask your insurer what rating applies to your address and keep the answer with your sale documents.

Unpaid taxes turn delinquent April 1, with certificates sold by June 1. After two years a holder can apply for a tax deed with a $75 application fee, and the clerk runs the auction.

The opening bid on a homestead includes one half of the latest assessed value. If you are behind, ask the Broward tax collector for a payoff and weigh a sale before a deed application.

  • Installment prepayment requires an application by May 1.
  • Senior deferral uses Form DR-570 by March 31.

Owners 65 or older may get an additional exemption of up to $50,000 if the local ordinance allows and income is within limit. A disabled veteran may receive a $5,000 assessed value reduction, and a person 65 or older with a service-connected disability may get a discount equal to the VA percentage.

Deployed servicemembers may receive an exemption proportional to the time deployed, and may rent out a homestead without abandoning it. Ask the property appraiser what proof is needed. These breaks stay with you and do not pass to the buyer.

sections.h2: Risks of an informal family transfer
sections.html: Moving legal or beneficial title counts as a change of ownership for assessment, with exceptions for spouses and some transfers at death, and quit claim deeds carry stamp tax. A deed must be a written conveyance signed before two witnesses, so have a title agent prepare it.

Once you accept, a title agent searches title, gathers payoffs and drafts the deed, which needs two witnesses. The clerk then records it and collects the tax.

  • Put the doc stamp payer in the contract.
  • Order mortgage payoff and association statements.
  • Check your exemption status before the tax split.
  • Have permit and inspection records ready for the buyer's inspector.

Start with paperwork. Collect your deed, the latest tax bill, any association documents, and permit records for roofs, windows or additions. Then weigh a listing, a private sale and a cash offer by your net proceeds. Insist on a written offer and read every line. If a cash buyer offers, ask for a closing date in writing and confirm the buyer takes the house as is, so repair requests do not appear after inspection. Recent sales near you are easy to compare because Pembroke Pines is large, so ask an agent for a short list before you set a price.

faqs.a: On January 16, 1960, when it was a village of about 1,500 people.

faqs.q: What doc stamp rate does Pembroke Pines use?
faqs.a: Seventy cents per $100 of consideration paid, the rate that applies across Broward.

faqs.q: Can I keep my Save Our Homes savings?
faqs.a: Possibly. Portability may carry as much as $500,000 of the difference to a new Florida homestead.
Under the state rule each party stays liable, so write the payer into the contract.

faqs.q: Is an inherited Pembroke Pines house taxed when it transfers?
faqs.a: A personal representative's deed under a probated will is not taxed, while other transfers can be, so check with a title agent.
